newsitem.title: UK: Dollar vaults hurdles, bourses end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Dollar vaults hurdles, bourses end mixed.

text.p: The dollar broke through 118 yen for the first time in almost four years on Monday and vaulted important hurdles against the mark and Swiss franc.
On the bourses, leading German shares ignored another overnight stock plunge in Tokyo and were boosted by the higher dollar to a record closing high.

French stocks also hit a new peak in morning trading before falling back to end lower, along with London, on profit-taking, nervousness ahead of testimony on Tuesday by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan and a weaker Wall Street.
The Dow Jones industrial average of U.S. blue-chip share prices was down 25 points at 6,808.85 by the time London closed.

Bloodletting in Tokyo, where the Nikkei average fell 3.37 percent overnight, weakened the Japanese currency and by late Monday morning a robust dollar had broken above 118 yen to levels not seen since March 1993.
By the end of European trading it was slightly off its highs but dealers said dollar sentiment was still firm and it could move higher in coming days.

The dollar also marched ahead against the mark, breaking briefly above 1.6300 marks to levels not seen since June 1994 as speculation increased of a possible German interest rate cut. It later slipped to close in Europe at around 1.6255.

"The mark came under intense pressure in Europe, which gave added impetus to the firm dollar," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro in London. "After such a rally, it's due for a bit of a setback."
The dollar's strength across the board also led it to break through 1.42 Swiss francs and 5.50 against the French franc for the first time since summer 1994.
In contrast, the mark weakened against other European currencies. It fell to a 31-month low against the lira and continued to slide against the Norwegian crown.

"It will be a continuation of two themes. The U.S. economy is growing well and it's a question of when, rather than whether, the Fed will raise rates," said IBJ International chief analyst Keith Edmonds.
"On the other side of the interest rate equation, the groundwork is being laid for a German interest rate cut."
Analysts said the dollar's rise had been checked somewhat by a partial U.S. holiday for Martin Luther King Day. U.S. stock exchanges and the New York Mercantile Exchange were operating normally.

In Frankfurt, German shares ended bourse trade at a new record high, with the DAX index up almost one percent at 3,030.68 points, propelled by the strongly higher dollar, which makes German exports more attractive.

Traders said, however, they were wary about further gains in the DAX amid expectations of correction and bouts of profit-taking. The IBIS DAX index, which reflects all-day computer dealings, ended down about a quarter percent under the influence of the softer Dow.

London, Europe's busiest bourse, retreated from its record close on Friday to end at the day's lows, influenced by Wall Street. Analysts said the market was cautious ahead of Greenspan's speech and profit-taking hit several big gainers from last week.
The FTSE 100 index ended a third of a percentage point down at 4,194.0. Volume was a relatively subdued 384 million shares.
French stocks also closed lower after the market tracked the early decline on Wall Street due to profit-taking.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 19 points, or 0.78 percent, at 2,406.10 after giving up an early advance that lifted it an all-time intraday high of 2,438.50 points.
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was trading at 118.04 yen and 1.6255 marks compared with Friday's late European levels of 117.26 and 1.6135.
STOCK MARKETS
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 13.7 points lower at 4,194.0.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 19.00 at 2,406.10. The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 29.31 at 3,030.68.
In New York the Dow Jones Average was down 25 at 6,808.25
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $353.60 compared with a $355.15 close in London on Friday. Silver finished three cents lower at $4.75.
